blockers.quote: And tonight, the whole city is in one room.
blockers.why: #5 But / therefore: the stadium arrives as an “and then” spectacle rather than a consequence of the screen limitation.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Not on a screen. Only in the room. So you go to the biggest room in the city.”

blockers.quote: Over every head you can see, a counter: lies since midnight.
blockers.why: #16 A flagged limit that pays off: the rule runs for four spoken lines, past the three-line maximum.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 63–67 with two lines: “Over every head: lies spoken since midnight. It clicks on a lie and resets at midnight.” / “Jokes and honest mistakes don't count.” Keep the planted line 69 unchanged as the third line.

blockers.quote: The sink is full. You laugh, and you don't say a word.
blockers.why: #11 Never say the feeling and #12 Leave fast: this repeats the performed shot, while the final image lacks the required real-world residue.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Tomorrow, when you say you're fine, listen for the click.” Keep line 481, then shorten line 483 to: “Would you want to see your own number? Tell us.”

suggestions.quote: Fifty-one. It's still in his drafts. You wait at his desk until he sends it.
suggestions.fix: Let the win turn against you: he sends the proposal, then removes your name before it leaves. That gives the beat a value loss and motivates taking the power outside work.

suggestions.quote: Can this spread? You don't know. You don't know how you got it.
suggestions.fix: Tie the question directly to the planted stranger: “Someone else is counting the box exactly as you are. Maybe the power isn't yours alone.”

keep.quote: The city isn't lying to you. The city is mostly fine. The few who are have a corner office.
Host: Read it out loud. For the people who can't see.
That's nine. And he's the honest one.
